title: Water Safety/Survival Instructor (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, CG TECOM
raw_text:
7.     MOS 0918, Water Safety/Survival Instructor (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, CG TECOM

    a. Summary. Marine Corps Instructors of water survival train and equip
Marines with the requisite knowledge and skills to successfully negotiate
water obstacles and survive in emergency situations in aquatic environments.
Additionally, they employ water survival skills of increasing levels of
ability designed to reduce fear, raise self-confidence, and develop Marines
with the ability to survive in water.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be the grade of E-4 or above.

            (2) Must possess a current 1st class PFT/CFT.

            (3) Must complete all aquatic events required by the NAVMC 11627.

            (4) Must have at least one year of obligated service time remaining.

        (5) Must have a current water survival intermediate swim
qualification or higher.

    c. Requirements. Complete one of the CG TRNGCOM approved Marine Corps
Instructor of Water Survival Courses (N30L9N1, N30L9NM, M03L9N6, or M03L9NM)
at Expeditionary Warfare Training Group Pacific in San Diego, CA or Marine
Corps Water Survival School in Camp Lejeune, NC.

    d. Duties. Responsible for developing, planning, conducting, and
supervising Marine Corps Water Survival training and qualifications. For a
partial listing of duties and tasks, refer to MCO 1500.52 and NAVMC 3500.33.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

Occupational Field 09, Training, comprises MOSs used to identify Marines who possess skill sets to conduct vital training, particularly to entry-level Marines, as required by various high visibility Marine Corps programs. First exposure to Marine Corps training is provided by the Drill Instructor. Next contact is with the marksmanship coaches and instructors overseen by a Range Officer, Swim Instructors, Martial Arts Instructors, and then Marine Combat Instructors. In the operating forces, training continues with the addition of Small Weapons Instructors and Martial Arts Instructor-Trainers. These MOSs are sponsored by the Training and Education Command.

7. MOS 0918, Water Safety/Survival Instructor (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, CG TECOM a. Summary. Marine Corps Instructors of water survival train and equip Marines with the requisite knowledge and skills to successfully negotiate water obstacles and survive in emergency situations in aquatic environments. Additionally, they employ water survival skills of increasing levels of ability designed to reduce fear, raise self-confidence, and develop Marines with the ability to survive in water. b. Prerequisites (1) Must be the grade of E-4 or above. (2) Must possess a current 1st class PFT/CFT. (3) Must complete all aquatic events required by the NAVMC 11627. (4) Must have at least one year of obligated service time remaining. (5) Must have a current water survival intermediate swim qualification or higher. c. Requirements. Complete one of the CG TRNGCOM approved Marine Corps Instructor of Water Survival Courses (N30L9N1, N30L9NM, M03L9N6, or M03L9NM) at Expeditionary Warfare Training Group Pacific in San Diego, CA or Marine Corps Water Survival School in Camp Lejeune, NC. d. Duties. Responsible for developing, planning, conducting, and supervising Marine Corps Water Survival training and qualifications. For a partial listing of duties and tasks, refer to MCO 1500.52 and NAVMC 3500.33.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
